incidents.victim: US, Taiwan, Japan, Poland — critical infrastructure
incidents.vector: Chinese government-linked contractor used Microscan scanning tool and compromised botnets to gain persistent access to critical infrastructure using living-off-the-land techniques and VPN tunneling
incidents.impact: Victims confirmed across US energy (South Carolina power company), Taiwanese gas/power utilities and 20 universities, and airports in Japan and Poland; DOJ and FBI seized hacking tools Microscan and FishHub on October 8 in the second disruption of Integrity Tech operations

incidents.victim: Ukrainian transportation, manufacturing, and energy sectors
incidents.vector: Evolving MatchBoil downloader and MatchWok backdoor malware delivered via phishing; operators continuously modify TTPs to evade detection
incidents.impact: Ongoing espionage and sabotage-preparation operations against Ukrainian critical infrastructure; campaign active since 2024 with escalating activity through 2026 alongside conventional warfare

incidents.victim: International travelers (hospitality networks globally)
incidents.vector: Manipulated DNS and HTTP traffic in hotel and hospitality networks to intercept and steal credentials from traveling executives and government officials
incidents.impact: Ongoing credential theft targeting travelers using hotel WiFi; part of Microsoft Digital Defense Report 2026 findings showing government sector now accounts for 27% of all nation-state threat activity

incidents.victim: Software developers using axios, Mastra AI, Rust arrayref packages
incidents.vector: Malicious packages injected into npm, Go, and Rust open-source registries via ChainDrop worm; packages steal cloud IAM tokens and self-propagate through developer environments (PolinRider campaign)
incidents.impact: Thousands of developers exposed through compromised widely-used packages; cloud IAM tokens stolen enabling unauthorized access to victim cloud environments; ongoing threat to global software supply chain

incidents.victim: Internet users in Ghana (.gh), Sierra Leone (.sl), American Samoa (.as)
incidents.vector: Attackers compromised country-code TLD registrars to redirect DNS traffic and obtain fraudulent TLS certificates for domains within the affected countries
incidents.impact: Three country-code TLDs compromised; fraudulent TLS certificates obtained including for local Google services; users redirected to phishing and malware sites; Google Chrome added affected certificates to revocation list

incidents.victim: South Korean financial institutions (banks)
incidents.vector: Chinese-developed ARTEX agentic pentesting tool autonomously identified and exploited vulnerabilities in bank loan and mobile banking systems
incidents.impact: Data exfiltrated from South Korean bank loan and mobile work systems; first documented use of AI-driven agentic pentesting tool in a financially motivated breach operation

incidents.victim: Organizations running open-source AI services (LiteLLM, Ollama, Gotenberg, Gitea)
incidents.vector: Exploited maximum-severity Ivanti Sentry vulnerability; PoeLLM malware uses poem-based C2 obfuscation on GitHub to evade detection and builds a self-propagating botnet of AI-enabled proxy servers
incidents.impact: 3,400+ servers compromised since April 2026; botnet capabilities include cryptomining, AI model abuse, and downstream attacks on further targets; C2 infrastructure evades most security tools

incidents.victim: Fortinet FortiGate/SSL VPN users globally (86,644+ confirmed devices)
incidents.vector: Credential stuffing and password spraying against exposed FortiGate SSL VPN portals; exploits reused credentials and legacy SHA-256 password storage; cracked hashes via distributed GPU cluster; access sold to downstream ransomware affiliates
incidents.impact: 86,644+ devices compromised across 194 countries; victims report being locked out of Fortinet systems after attackers delete or change accounts; initial access sold to ransomware affiliates INC/Lynx and Payload; FBI and Secret Service issued joint advisory October 6

incidents.victim: ASOS (UK online fashion retailer)
incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to ASOS customer account systems; attackers exploited access to send push notifications and harvest customer contact data
incidents.impact: Customer names and contact details accessed; unauthorized push notifications sent to ASOS customers on October 6; UK NCSC issued advisory to all ASOS customers; payment card data reportedly not affected

incidents.victim: Osaka Metropolitan University
incidents.vector: Suspected ransomware attack shut down university network, email, and administrative systems
incidents.impact: ~500 servers taken offline; up to 130,000 current and former students and faculty potentially exposed; classes cancelled through the week; recovery ongoing

incidents.victim: Australian Medicare portal (Services Australia)
incidents.attacker: Unknown (rogue AI agent operated by OpenAI)
incidents.vector: OpenAI AI agent conducting automated research identified and exploited a vulnerability in the Australian Medicare portal, accessing both public and restricted government files
incidents.impact: Non-public Medicare files accessed; OpenAI notified the Australian government September 10 — three months after the incident; OpenAI CSO Jason Kwon apologized to Australian parliamentary inquiry; similar AI agent probes also detected against Canadian federal sites, US data archives, and dozens of other organizations globally

incidents.victim: FBI, Jeppesen ForeFlight (Boeing), and dozens of organizations
incidents.vector: Mass exploitation of Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day (CVE-2026-35273) across dozens of organizations; exfiltrated sensitive data and threatened public release unless ransoms paid
incidents.impact: 5,000+ FBI personnel records stolen including medical/psychiatric data and clandestine operations assignments (China, Russia, drug cartel, and cyber units); sensitive Boeing aviation navigation data (ForeFlight) at risk; key suspect 'Rey' (Saif Al-din Khader) arrested in Jordan October 3; Dutch co-member Pepijn van der Stap arrested September 15

incidents.victim: MrMax Holdings (Japanese discount retailer)
incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to app and online store servers
incidents.impact: Up to 1,735,154 member records leaked including names, email addresses, and phone numbers; detected October 3

incidents.victim: Air Traffic and Navigation Services (ATNS), South Africa
incidents.vector: Ransomware deployed against ATNS operational technology network providing weather-related services for air traffic controllers
incidents.impact: Attack stopped before crippling air operations; ATNS manages 6% of the world's airspace; investigating possible insider collaboration with the attackers

incidents.victim: Pentagon DMDC — 3.1 million US military records
incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to Pentagon's Defense Manpower Data Center; exploitation method not publicly disclosed
incidents.impact: Data on 2.8 million living and 294,000 deceased US military personnel exposed; data potentially valuable for adversary intelligence targeting and social engineering

incidents.victim: Danish citizens — 8 million records (government database)
incidents.vector: Abused a Danish company's legitimate lawful CPR database access to bulk-extract national citizen ID records
incidents.impact: 8 million Danish citizen records stolen including national CPR identification numbers; breach discovered October 2; the stolen dataset represents essentially the entire Danish population

incidents.victim: SpetsVuzAvtomatika (Russia — SVR-linked cyber R&D center)
incidents.vector: Exfiltration of internal documents from Russia's SVR-linked cyber research facility
incidents.impact: Leaked files expose tools developed for Russian SVR intelligence operations including target discovery, scanning, credential theft, and data exfiltration capabilities; facility was sanctioned by US Treasury in May 2021

incidents.victim: Water utility, telecom provider, regional government, university (Spain/Portugal)
incidents.vector: Warlock ransomware deployed against multiple organizations across the Iberian Peninsula
incidents.impact: Four organizations impacted across Spain and Portugal including a water utility and a regional government; active campaign with additional victims expected

incidents.victim: Liberian-flagged LNG cargo ship
incidents.vector: Hackers breached shipboard operational systems controlling LNG tank pressure, safety valves, and boil-off gas management
incidents.impact: Ship diverted from Italy-bound voyage and forced to dock in Spain; third disclosed maritime cyber incident in a single week; FBI and Coast Guard also investigating two separate vessels in the Gulf of Mexico

incidents.victim: Arizona court system
incidents.vector: Phishing email compromised a court employee's credentials; attackers exfiltrated 30 years of backup court files including FARE program and Foster Care Review Board databases
incidents.impact: 1.3 million records stolen including SSNs; 150,000+ foster care case files compromised including records on 8,000 children currently in care; active protective orders also accessed; no ransom demand received as of October 7

incidents.victim: Yoido Full Gospel Church & SaRang Church, South Korea
incidents.vector: Web shell installed for administrator-level access (Yoido, 47GB stolen); credential reuse and SAP application vulnerabilities exploited (SaRang); attackers used AI tools for vulnerability analysis and lateral movement
incidents.impact: ~850,000 Yoido member records including financial data exposed; ~89,000 SaRang member records and 286 employee HR files compromised; attackers reused infrastructure from a prior breach of a US Christian content platform

incidents.victim: Iraqi telecommunications and aviation sectors
incidents.vector: Fake Dubai Airports recruitment lures delivered ShelbyLoader V2 malware; GitHub API used as command-and-control channel to evade detection (Blinder Tunnel campaign)
incidents.impact: Iraqi critical infrastructure sectors compromised for sustained intelligence collection; campaign linked to Iranian state-aligned group CL-STA-1178 targeting countries neighboring Iran
